ai.text:
The European Business Wallets proposal aims to make it simpler and safer for businesses and public authorities across the EU to deal with each other online. It is meant to reduce administrative burdens, streamline compliance, and improve how public services are delivered, and it builds on the EU's existing digital identity framework.

The proposal sets up a framework for providing these wallets and gives actions carried out through them the same legal effect as those done in person, on paper, or by other compliant means. It also sets rules for issuing identification data to business and public-sector wallet owners, and it creates a European Digital Directory run by the European Commission. Wallet owners would be identified with the existing European unique identifier (EUID), or a similar identifier where the EUID is not available.

Under the proposal, providers of these wallets would have to notify authorities before operating, and public sector bodies would have specific obligations concerning the wallets. A supervision framework would apply where public bodies provide the wallets. The proposal also allows recognition of similar systems from outside the EU and the issuing of wallets to non-EU businesses, so that trusted cross-border exchanges with international partners can take place.

The use of European Digital Identity Wallets by individuals is voluntary. People who do not use them may not be restricted or disadvantaged in accessing public or private services, the labour market, or the freedom to conduct business, and other existing identification methods remain available.
